result.rationale: Verifiable from the diff: the embedding.hbs template only renders a table and an add_host button — no control invokes saveChanges; the controller's saveChanges calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, and Admin::EmbeddingController#update just re-renders the serialized embedding without persisting anything. So both client action and PUT endpoint are present-but-no-op code, a concrete maintainability/data-loss trap for anyone wiring up a save button. Not incorrect current behavior, so not a bug, but a substantive, specific review concern.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines an action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would hit the new PUT route (`put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`). However, `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` has no button or UI element wired to `saveChanges` (only `addHost` and per-host save/delete actions). On the server, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders the serializer and does not persist any params (it doesn’t modify settings or records). This is not a currently user-visible defect since there are no embedding-level fields being edited in the template, but it is dead/no-op plumbing that could mislead maintainers if they later add a save button expecting persistence.
